security_spec.violation_condition: In the FreeBSD kernel, when Sspmpsw is implemented, a context switch writes sspmpswitch to activate the incoming thread's SPMP entries and deactivate the outgoing thread's entries, but the code path omits the mandatory SFENCE.VMA (rs1=x0, rs2=x0) after the CSR write — allowing subsequent S-mode memory accesses (load/store/instruction fetch) to be reordered before the sspmpswitch write takes effect.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: csrw sspmpswitch.*(?!SFENCE\.VMA|sfence_vma)|writes to sspmpswitch CSR not immediately followed by SFENCE.VMA with rs1=x0 and rs2=x0 before any subsequent load, store, or instruction fetch in the same code path
security_spec.summary: Writes to sspmpswitch during SPMP context switch require a subsequent SFENCE.VMA(x0, x0) fence to order SPMP entry activation with memory accesses; omitting it creates a window where the old thread's memory protections are lifted before the new thread's are enforced, enabling cross-process memory access

findings.finding: No SPMP CSR address constants defined. Only M-mode PMP CSRs (CSR_PMPCFG0-3 at 0x3a0, CSR_PMPADDR0-15 at 0x3b0) exist. Missing: CSR_SISELECT (0x150), CSR_SIREG (0x151), CSR_SIREG2 (0x152), CSR_SPMPCFG0-3 (0x1a0), CSR_SPMPADDR0-15 (0x1b0), CSR_SSPMPSWITCH, CSR_SSPMPSWITCHH, CSR_MENVCFG (0x30a), CSR_SENVCFG (0x10a), CSR_MSECCFG (0x747). Without CSR address constants, no code can reference sspmpswitch — the vulnerability pattern of 'csrw sspmpswitch not followed by SFENCE.VMA' cannot occur.
findings.snippet:
#define CSR_PMPCFG0 0x3a0
#define CSR_PMPCFG1 0x3a1
#define CSR_PMPCFG2 0x3a2
#define CSR_PMPCFG3 0x3a3
#define CSR_PMPADDR0 0x3b0
// ... PMPADDR1-15 continue to 0x3bf
// No SPMP CSR constants exist anywhere in this file

findings.finding: HENVCFG bit definitions include STCE (bit 63), PBMTE (bit 62), CBZE/CBCFE/CBIE (bits 4-7), FIOM (bit 0). Missing: HENVCFG_SSE (bit 3) which controls SPMP enable for VS-mode. Also entirely absent: MENVCFG_SSE, SENVCFG_SSE, and all MENVCFG/SENVCFG bit definitions. Without the SSE bit, no privilege level can enable SPMP.
findings.snippet:
#define HENVCFG_STCE   (1ULL << 63)
#define HENVCFG_PBMTE  (1ULL << 62)
#define HENVCFG_CBZE   (1ULL << 7)
#define HENVCFG_CBCFE  (1ULL << 6)
#define HENVCFG_CBIE   (0x3ULL << 4)
#define HENVCFG_FIOM   (1ULL << 0)
// Missing: HENVCFG_SSE (bit 3)

findings.finding: ISA extension detection defines smode_extensions bitmap with SV_SSTC, SV_SVNAPOT, SV_SVPBMT, SV_SVINVAL, SV_SSCOFPMF. No slot for Smspmp, Sspmp, Sspmpss, Smnpm, Ssnpm, or Smepmp. The kernel cannot discover whether hardware supports SPMP.
findings.snippet:
static const struct isa_ext smode_extensions[] = {
    ISA_EXT(SV_SSTC),
    ISA_EXT(SV_SVNAPOT),
    ISA_EXT(SV_SVPBMT),
    ISA_EXT(SV_SVINVAL),
    ISA_EXT(SV_SSCOFPMF),
    // No SPMP-related extension slot

findings.finding: pmap_activate_sw() handles address-space switching: csr_write(satp, ...) at line 5187, then CPU_SET/CPU_CLR/PCPU_SET bookkeeping (loads/stores, lines 5189-5197), then sfence_vma() at line 5199. No SPMP context-switch logic exists. No sspmpswitch CSR write exists to evaluate for the SFENCE.VMA ordering requirement. The existing sfence_vma() would cover SPMP visibility IF sspmpswitch were written before it — but no such write exists.

fork_trampoline is the new-process entry to U-mode. Calls fork_exit() (line 369), restores sstatus/sepc/GPRs/sscratch, then sret (line 431). No sfence.vma appears before sret. If SPMP were implemented and fork_exit() configured thread-specific SPMP entries, the sret would lack the required fence before entering U-mode. Currently harmless because no SPMP configuration occurs.

User trap-return path: do_trap_user → do_ast → load_registers → sret. No sfence.vma in this path. If do_trap_user/do_ast were to reprogram SPMP (e.g., during preemption or signal delivery), the sret would execute without the SPMP visibility fence. load_registers performs CSR writes (sstatus, sepc, sscratch) and GPR loads but no sfence.vma. Currently harmless because no SPMP manipulation occurs.
findings.snippet:
ENTRY(cpu_exception_handler_user)
    save_registers 0
    mv a0, sp
    call _C_LABEL(do_trap_user)
    do_ast
    load_registers 0
    csrrw sp, sscratch, sp
    sret

findings.finding: Supervisor trap-return path: do_trap_supervisor → load_registers → sret. No sfence.vma in this path. If do_trap_supervisor were to reprogram SPMP, the sret would lack the required fence. Currently harmless because no SPMP manipulation occurs.
findings.snippet:
ENTRY(cpu_exception_handler_supervisor)
    save_registers 1
    mv a0, sp
    call _C_LABEL(do_trap_supervisor)
    load_registers 1
    sret

findings.finding: Restores guest VM CSRs: vsstatus, vsie, vstvec, vsscratch, vsepc, vscause, vstval, hvip, vsatp. No SFENCE.VMA follows the vsatp write (line 176) — a pre-existing gap. Also, the senvcfg field in struct hypcsr (riscv.h:67) exists but is never written here. If SPMP were added, any sspmpswitch write here would also be unfenced, and the guest's SPMP enable state would be lost across VM exit/entry.

Saves guest CSRs on VM exit but does not read vsenvcfg (missing at line 194). If guest sets senvcfg.SSE to enable SPMP for VS-mode, that state is silently discarded. The stored hypcsr.senvcfg field (riscv.h:67) remains stale/zero, and vmmops_vcpu_restore_csrs never writes senvcfg — so guest SPMP enable state is lost across VM exit.

VMM guest entry sequence: hfence_gvma() (G-stage only) → csr_write(hgatp, ...) → csr_write(henvcfg, HENVCFG_STCE) (SSE bit never set) → vmmops_vcpu_restore_csrs (restores vsatp without SFENCE.VMA) → vmm_fence_process (no SPMP fence type) → vmm_switch. henvcfg.SSE is never set, so even if hardware supports SPMP, the hypervisor never enables it for VS-mode. No SFENCE.VMA or HFENCE.VVMA for VS-stage state.

Host↔guest world-switch in assembly. Performs atomic CSR swaps for sstatus, hstatus, scounteren, sscratch, stvec, sepc (lines 73-78), loads all guest GPRs (lines 86-118), executes sret (line 120) into the guest VM. Contains ZERO fence instructions — no sfence.vma, no hfence.gvma, no hfence.vvma. All fences must be provided by the caller. If sspmpswitch were written in vmmops_vcpu_restore_csrs (called before vmm_switch), the guest's first instruction fetch and all subsequent loads/stores could observe stale SPMP state.

VMM fence queue system only handles FENCE_I (line 135) and FENCE_VMA/FENCE_VMA_ASID (lines 95-121). Enum vmm_fence_type (riscv.h:70-75) defines only VMM_RISCV_FENCE_I, VMM_RISCV_FENCE_VMA, VMM_RISCV_FENCE_VMA_ASID. vmm_fence_process() processes FENCE_REQ_I and FENCE_REQ_VMA. No VMM_RISCV_FENCE_SPMP type, no HFENCE.VVMA support, no infrastructure to synchronize guest SPMP visibility across vCPUs. The KASSERT at line 95 only accepts VMA and VMA_ASID fence types.
